subject: chemistry
question_text: Write an expression for the kinetic energy of a gas molecule.

mark_split.label: Derivation from the kinetic gas equation

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 2+2 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. TITLE VS ANSWER: the book's title asks the kinetic energy of a gas MOLECULE, but its model answer derives the per-MOLE expression (3/2)RT and stops there. The card derives per mole as the book does and adds the per-molecule form (3/2)kT, so the answer also matches the title. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. The derivation ⅓MU² → ⅔Eₖ = RT → Eₖ = (3/2)RT and the per-molecule form (3/2)kT are both correct. Added one sentence to the final step's why saying (3/2)RT is the TRANSLATIONAL kinetic energy — the kinetic gas equation models a molecule as a moving point — so a student who knows a diatomic molecule also rotates is not told the card is wrong. No marked line changed.

steps.label: Derivation from the kinetic gas equation
lines: For 1 mole: mn = M (molar mass), so PV = ⅓ MU²
For 1 mole of an ideal gas: PV = RT   … (2)
steps.why: ½MU² is the kinetic energy of one mole, so PV is rewritten to expose it: ⅓ = ⅔ × ½. Setting the result against PV = RT eliminates PV and ties the kinetic energy directly to temperature.
common_mistakes: Losing the ⅔ factor when converting ⅓MU² into kinetic-energy form.
Using PV = nRT here — for ONE mole the right side is RT.
steps.memory_tip: Split one third into two thirds times one half; the one half forms the kinetic energy term.
steps.margin_note: Numbering the two equations and combining them is the structure the examiner rewards.

steps.label: The expressions

lines.text: Eₖ = (3/2) RT per mole ;  for n moles Eₖ = (3/2) nRT

lines: Per molecule: divide by the Avogadro number N,
steps.why: Rearranging ⅔Eₖ = RT gives the per-mole energy (3/2)RT, and dividing by the number of molecules in a mole scales it to one molecule, where R/N is Boltzmann's constant k. This is the TRANSLATIONAL kinetic energy: the kinetic gas equation treats a molecule as a moving point, so (3/2)RT is the expected answer for every gas, monatomic or diatomic.
common_mistakes: Stopping at (3/2)RT when the question says molecule — add (3/2)kT.
Writing (2/3) in the final expression instead of (3/2).
steps.memory_tip: Three halves R T per mole; swap R for k and the same shape is per molecule.
steps.margin_note: The n-mole and per-molecule lines make the expression usable in every numerical of this chapter.

insider_note: The question says molecule but most model answers stop at (3/2)RT per mole — writing (3/2)kT as the per-molecule line is the difference between following the book and answering the question.
